name: Sydney
description: Central Sydney from open data, lit by the real sun. Every shadow is computed, and every height is traceable to its source.

terrain.attribution: NSW Spatial Services NSW_5M_Elevation, 5 m bare earth from stereo imagery (CC BY 4.0)

water.note: Sydney Harbour is mapped as a water polygon (Port Jackson); the Overture ocean polygon stops at the Heads.

waves.note: A typical afternoon north-easterly sea breeze over the 4 km reach from Bradleys Head to the bridge; chosen values, not a measurement.

water.colour_note: Harbour water is green-brown with a few metres of visibility; the colours were picked from the NSW aerial photo.

protection.title: Sydney LEP 2012, clause 6.18
protection.summary: Development may not add to the total shadow on these public places across their protected hours.
protection.source_note: Protected windows as amended by Amendment No 64. The NSW legislation site refused automated access, so they were transcribed from secondary sources; check the official text before relying on them. Places without a verified window show sun now but are not tested.
protection.reading_note: Two readings matter more than any data error. Times: the Standard Time Act 1987 is reported to read times in legal instruments as standard time, which during daylight saving is an hour later on the clock; for Macquarie Place that changes the sun in its window by up to 44 points. Baseline: the clause compares against buildings existing at a fixed date, while this test compares against today's model.
protection.tip: Tip: try the block west of Hyde Park, or just north of Martin Place.

reference_heights.source: Wikipedia, List of tallest buildings in Sydney (October 2026)

tour.title: Central Sydney from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap via Overture Maps, standing on NSW 5 m bare-earth terrain under NSW aerial imagery.

tour.title: Sydney Opera House
tour.text: Each shell is a spherical triangle cut from one sphere of radius 75.2 m, the rule Utzon settled on in 1961. The highest shell stands 67 m above sea level.

tour.title: Sydney Harbour Bridge
tour.text: Arch span 503 m, crown 134 m above sea level, 28 panels. The alignment comes from the two pylon footprints in OpenStreetMap, {landmark:harbour_bridge.bearing_deg}° east of north.

tour.title: A winter day on the towers
tour.text: 21 June, 8 am to 4 pm. The sun never climbs above 32.7° here, so at noon a 200 m tower casts a shadow over 310 m long.

tour.title: Martin Place at lunchtime
tour.text: On 21 June at 12:30, {sun:Martin Place|6-21|12:30}% of Martin Place gets direct sun; on 21 December, {sun:Martin Place|12-21|12:30}%. The plan protects it only from 1 September to 31 May, 12:00–14:00.

tour.title: Hyde Park in its protected hours
tour.text: Protected all year from 10:00 to 14:00. On the winter solstice, sun on the park falls from {sun:Hyde Park|6-21|10:00}% at 10:00 to {sun:Hyde Park|6-21|14:00}% at 14:00 as the towers to the west take over.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: surveyed, published or verified height. Orange: floor count × storey height. Green: estimated. Against {acc:matched} published tower heights the median error is {acc:median_abs_error_pct}%.

tour.title: After dark
tour.text: Windows light from the same facade grid that shades them by day. Drag to explore, or open Sun access to test a tower of your own.

sources.landmarks: Sydney Opera House and Sydney Harbour Bridge published dimensions

game.title: Sydney on Foot
game.under_bridge_note: 49 m of clearance, and you used it.

ferry_style.note: Sydney Ferries' green and cream with a gold band; the dimensions are approximate.

game.ferry_note: Wharves and the helipad are from OpenStreetMap via Overture. Routes are generated through open water, and the stops follow the inner-harbour services, but the timetable is not real. Ferries run at 1.5 times their real speed (9 m/s) and wait 20 s at each wharf. The vessel names are those of the First Fleet class ferries. At a wharf you can skip the wait.

vehicles.note: The helicopter, ferries and cars are shared by every city (web/assets/vehicles, built by blender/build_vehicles.py). Pick a livery from vehicles.json or give your own colours; the registration defaults to the country's. The ferries take their colours and length from ferry_style.

cars.note: Sydney's taxis come in any colour, mostly white, silver or black, with a roof sign; the buses are white with a blue band (approximate).

npcs.name: Ava
idle: The whole model is open data. If something looks wrong, it probably is wrong in the data, so tell me.

npcs.name: Marco
idle: Each shell is a triangle cut from one sphere, 75.2 m in radius. Utzon's 'spherical solution', 1961.

npcs.name: Lena
idle: The arch spans 503 m. The deck is {landmark:harbour_bridge.deck_width_m} m wide and 49 m above the water.

npcs.name: Sam
idle: Under the deck, keep it below 45 m. The rotor needs the room.

npcs.name: Priya
idle: Martin Place is protected from 1 September to 31 May, 12:00 to 14:00. Winter isn't covered.

npcs.name: Tom
idle: A floor count times a storey height beats a machine-learning guess most of the time. Not always.

npcs.name: Noor
idle: Barangaroo Reserve was a container wharf until 2015. Now it's sandstone and fig trees.

npcs.name: Kev
idle: Bream under the bridge in the mornings. {sun_line}

quests.title: Welcome to the Quay
talk: You're the new surveyor? Good. This city is rebuilt from open data: {buildings} buildings, real terrain, the real sun.
Before we check anything, get your bearings. Marco is on the Opera House forecourt. Walk over and say hello.
WASD or the arrow keys to move, Shift to sprint, X to walk, drag to look around. E to talk.

steps.text: Meet Marco on the Opera House forecourt

quests.title: Shells from one sphere
talk: Ava sent you? Welcome. Look up: every one of these shells is a spherical triangle cut from one sphere, 75.2 m in radius.
The highest shell stands 67 m above sea level. The model builds them from that one rule, not from a scan.
First, climb the Monumental Steps up to the podium. They're nearly 100 m wide, and everyone who comes here sits on them.
Then see the harbour from the water. Take a ferry from Circular Quay, Wharf 4, to Milsons Point. Lena will meet you there.

steps.text: Climb the Monumental Steps to the podium
Take a ferry from Circular Quay to Milsons Point

quests.title: Over the arch
talk: Nice ride? Now look up. The arch spans 503 m, and its crown is 134 m above the water.
The deck in this model rises on its approach viaducts until it meets the ground. Walk up from here to the middle of the arch.

steps.text: Walk up onto the bridge and reach the middle of the arch
Meet Sam at the Kirribilli helipad

quests.title: Under the bridge
talk: Lena said you'd come. Hop in. The helicopter's on the pad.
Fly under the bridge deck. It clears the water by 49 m, so stay below 45. Then set down in the Domain. Priya's waiting near Martin Place.
Space to climb, C to descend, W and S for forward and back, A and D to turn. V switches to a bird's-eye view. E gets you out once you've landed.

steps.text: Fly under the Harbour Bridge deck

quests.title: A place in the sun
talk: The planning rule says new towers may not add shadow to Martin Place between 12:00 and 14:00, from September to May.
Winter isn't protected. On 21 June at 12:30, only {sun:Martin Place|6-21|12:30}% of the place gets direct sun. On 21 December it's {sun:Martin Place|12-21|12:30}%.
Find a sunny spot here at lunchtime on 21 June. Watch the sun meter under the map. It ray-casts from where you stand.

steps.text: Stand in direct sun in Martin Place, 12:00 to 14:00 on 21 June
Meet Tom at the north end of Hyde Park

quests.title: Where heights come from
talk: Every building here carries the source of its height. {share:floors}% of the footprint area comes from a floor count, {share:mapped}% from a surveyed height, and the rest is estimated.
Aim at a building and press Q to use the survey lens. Find one with a surveyed height, one from a floor count and one that's estimated.

steps.text: Survey lens (Q): a surveyed, a floor-count and an estimated height
Report back to Ava at Circular Quay

quests.title: Survey complete
talk: That's the full tour: the water, the bridge, the air, the sun and the data underneath it all.
{acc:matched} towers have been checked against their published heights, with a median error of {acc:median_abs_error_pct}%. Now you know where the other numbers come from.
The city is yours. Change the time of day, take any ferry, or fly anywhere.
